chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I not inform you about what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say when he retired to his bed?'

He said: 'He used to recite the Verse of the Chair (Ayat al-Kursi) and say: In the name of Allah, I believe in Allah and disbelieve in the idols (al-Taghut). O Allah, protect me in my sleep and in my waking.'

key_terms.وَ كَفَرْتُ بِالطَّاغُوتِ: And I disbelieve in the idols/evil powers

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say before sleeping according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this narration highlights the Prophet’s nightly routine of reciting Ayat al-Kursi alongside a concise declaration of faith and rejection of Taghut, emphasizing spiritual vigilance. The supplication for protection in both sleep and wakefulness underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining divine guardianship (Hifz) across all states of consciousness, bridging the gap between rest and action.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Shall I<sup>asws</sup> inform you with what Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to say whenever he<sup>saww</sup> retired to his<sup>saww</sup> bed?’

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>saww</sup> used to recite The Verse of the Chair (Ayat Al Kursy – 2:255) and he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘In the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. I<sup>saww</sup> believe in Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and disbelieve in the idols. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Protect me<sup>saww</sup> during my<sup>saww</sup> sleep and during my<sup>saww</sup> waking up’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Marwan who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) said, ‘Should I tell you about what the Messenger of Allah would say when going to his bed?’
The Imam said, ‘He would read verse 255 of Chapter two and say, “(I begin) in the name of Allah, I believe in Allah, and reject the devil. O Lord, protect me in my sleep and when I am awake.’”
